This is newly added code, so the defect is introduced by the diff: in credential-sharing mode, per-app schemas (googleCredentialSchema, refreshTokenResponseSchema, zoomRefreshedTokenSchema) are replaced by this broken minimal schema, allowing token responses without expiry fields to pass and causing stale expiry_date values in stored credentials.

judged_text: The computed keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] evaluate to identical literal stringified-schema property names, so minimumTokenResponseSchema implements none of its commented intent ('any property with a number is the expiry') and enforces nothing beyond access_token — no expiry property is ever validated. In sync mode a token response missing the expiry field parses successfully, so expiry_date/expires_in are never updated and office365/google credentials fail expiry checks or re-refresh on every operation, while the strict per-app schemas (googleCredentialSchema, refreshTokenResponseSchema, zoomRefreshedTokenSchema, salesforceTokenSchema) are silently discarded whenever the flag is on.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` is built with computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`. These evaluate to literal string keys (e.g., Zod’s stringified schema names), not an index signature/catchall, so the schema does not implement the intended “any numeric property is expiry” behavior. Instead it either (a) incorrectly requires a property with that literal key to exist (likely causing sync-mode parsing to fail and throw), and/or (b) never truly validates presence of an expiry field. Additionally, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` is set, the code intentionally switches from the per-app schema to this broken minimum schema, so strict validation is effectively bypassed/invalidated in that mode.
